picks.t: Noah Kahan – The Great Divide Tour
picks.d: Oracle Park is going to be absolutely electric this Friday — Noah Kahan is bringing his massive folk-pop anthems to the ballpark, with support from Gigi Perez and Annabelle Dinda. This show is sold out on the primary market, so check StubHub or Vivid Seats fast. One of the biggest nights of the summer, full stop.

picks.t: Daniel Caesar – Son of Spergy Tour
picks.d: Daniel Caesar closes out a two-night Chase Center run on Friday, and honestly this is one of the smoothest, most emotionally alive R&B shows you'll catch all year. His new album debuted at #1 on the Billboard R&B chart — his best yet — and 070 Shake is opening. Go.

picks.t: Off the Grid: Fort Mason Night Market
picks.d: Free entry, waterfront views, food trucks as far as the eye can see, craft vendors, and live music — this is the perfect warm-up to a big Friday night. Fort Mason's monthly night market is a genuine SF tradition and one of the best free hangs in the city.

picks.t: Fillmore After Dark: Hot August Night Block Party
picks.d: The Lower Fillmore shuts down for a classic car show, food trucks, local vendors, and live entertainment — all completely free. It's a neighborhood block party with serious SF soul, and it's happening right outside one of the most legendary music venues in America.

picks.t: Courtney Barnett – Creature of Habit Tour (2 Nights!)
picks.d: Two nights at the Fillmore from one of indie rock's sharpest wits — Courtney Barnett's deadpan storytelling and sprawling guitar work are a perfect match for this storied room. Wednesday from $76, Thursday from $81. If you can only do one night, go Wednesday.

picks.t: Jacob Hashimoto: Giant Arc Opens at SFMOMA
picks.d: A massive new site-specific installation opens this Saturday in SFMOMA's Roberts Family Gallery — and here's the best part: it's completely free, no ticket required. Hashimoto's large-scale kite-and-screen constructions are genuinely jaw-dropping in person.

picks.t: TRAIN – Drops of Jupiter: 25 Years in the Atmosphere
picks.d: SF's own Train is celebrating the 25th anniversary of Drops of Jupiter at Shoreline Amphitheatre — a genuine homecoming moment for one of the Bay's best-loved rock bands. Outdoor summer show, nostalgia cranked to eleven. Great date-night pick.

picks.t: Sunset Speed Dating – Ages 30–45 at Blackbird
picks.d: Jigsaw Dating takes over Blackbird for a proper evening of speed dating followed by a relaxed social hour — meet everyone in the room, then follow up with your favorites over drinks. Low pressure, well-run, and actually fun.
The SF Standard's free outdoor movie series is screening The Parent Trap this Friday — bring a blanket, bring snacks, bring someone cute. It's a San Francisco summer evening at its most charming.

Muse closes the week at Shoreline Amphitheatre with their signature sci-fi spectacle and catalog of stadium anthems. Tickets from $42 make this one of the best value big-show moments of the week — and Muse live is genuinely something to see.

picks.t: THROTTLE: OGUZ, NEUX, softchaos at 1015 Folsom
picks.d: Two rooms of heavy Berlin-inspired techno at SF's most iconic club night venue — NEUX and softchaos are both making their SF debuts, which means you get to tell people you saw them before everyone else did. Prepare for serious BPMs.

picks.t: Treasures of the Pharaohs at the de Young
picks.d: The de Young's blockbuster season show spans 3,000 years of ancient Egyptian civilization and runs through January — but this week is a great time to go before the summer crowds ease. Bay Area residents get free general admission every Saturday with valid ID.

picks.t: Mess Hall Food Hall Opens – The Presidio
picks.d: The Presidio's big new food hall brings a cafe, full bar, and three all-day restaurants under one roof — seafood, burgers, Korean, and tons of grab-and-go for a Tunnel Tops picnic. It's the coolest new lunch spot in the city right now.

ongoing.d: Sweeping career retrospective at SFMOMA for one of Latin America's most celebrated photographers — open now.

ongoing.t: Nengi Omuku: The Gathering – de Young
ongoing.d: Vibrant figurative paintings from the Nigerian-British artist, running through May 2028.
World-class exhibition of ancient Italian civilization, open through September 20.
SF's beloved sourdough baker finally has a brick-and-mortar — ube toast and sesame-scallion slices with morning coffee.
Free 2nd and 4th Saturday waterfront hangout with vendors and entertainment, through September.

new.name: JouJou
new.d: Oysters, caviar, champagne, and serious buzz from the True Laurel and Lazy Bear team — SF's splurgiest new opening.

new.name: Lucania
new.d: From the A16 team, with roasted sardines, mussels, pizza, pasta, and a killer Embarcadero patio at the old MarketBar space.

new.name: Rize Up Café
new.d: The farmers market legend goes brick-and-mortar with ube toast, sesame-scallion slices, and great coffee.

new.name: Mess Hall
new.d: Three all-day restaurants, a full bar, and grab-and-go for Tunnel Tops picnics — the Presidio's best new lunch move.

new.name: Bar Coto
new.d: Walk-in coffee, sandwiches, and summer gelato from the Cotogna crew — ideal for a Jackson Square afternoon.

classic.name: Bix
classic.d: Supper club glamour in a Gold Rush–era alley — the martinis and duck confit never miss.

classic.name: Dragon Beaux
classic.d: Elevated dim sum with beautiful presentations and killer shrimp dumplings — go for weekend brunch.

classic.name: Tony's Pizza Napoletana
classic.d: Award-winning, multiple-style pizza from Tony Gemignani — still the neighborhood anchor worth the wait.

classic.name: La Taqueria
classic.d: James Beard America's Classic, no rice in the burritos, and a Mission institution since 1973.

classic.name: Anchor Oyster Bar
classic.d: Old-school Castro institution for clam chowder, cold oysters, and a Dungeness crab louie.

classic.name: Marufuku Ramen
classic.d: Hakata-style tonkotsu with a rich broth that's earned a permanent line out the door — worth every minute.

bars.name: The DeLuxe
bars.d: Just resurrected from Club Deluxe's 2023 closure — improved sound system, classic cocktails, and nightly live music spanning genres.

bars.name: True Laurel
bars.d: The Lazy Bear bar spin-off with inventive seasonal cocktails and a low-key cool vibe — one of the best bars in the city, full stop.

bars.name: Zeitgeist
bars.d: Massive beer garden, cold pints, sausages, and zero pretension — the Mission's beloved outdoor hang.

bars.name: Bar Coto
bars.d: The Cotogna team's walk-in all-day bar — excellent wine list, gelato in summer, and a civilized afternoon vibe.

bars.name: Charmaine's at the Proper
bars.d: Rooftop views of the city skyline, strong cocktails, and that golden-hour SF light that makes everyone look good.

bars.name: Vesuvio Café
bars.d: Beat Generation legend next to City Lights bookstore — cheap drinks, great people-watching, and serious literary history.

bars.name: Andytown Coffee & Beer (Irving)
bars.d: Andytown's chill neighborhood outpost does excellent craft pints in the evening when the fog rolls in off the ocean.

bars.name: Brass Tacks
bars.d: Neighborhood cocktail bar with a relaxed vibe, strong drinks, and a crowd that's actually fun to talk to.

Sunday matinee to close out Boston

sports.note: Second in the Western Conference — a strong week and they clinch a playoff berth. Worth following closely.

concerts.t: Noah Kahan – The Great Divide Tour
concerts.d: Billions of streams, a reputation for one of the most electric live shows in music right now, and Oracle Park as his stage — Kahan brings support acts Gigi Perez and Annabelle Dinda along for the ride. This one sold out primary and it's not hard to see why. Check resale.

concerts.t: Daniel Caesar – Son of Spergy Tour
concerts.d: Night two of Caesar's Chase Center run — his new album hit #1 on the R&B charts and this is the smoothest, most soulful room you'll be in all week. Support from 070 Shake. Dress nice.

Hip-hop night at the Fillmore — an intimate setting for a genre that usually lives in bigger rooms. The Fillmore's sound system was basically built for exactly this, and the energy in that room on a Friday night is always something special.

A cross-genre double bill at the Fillmore — alternative indie from Little Stranger and reggae vibes from Tropidelic. Two distinct sounds, one legendary room, and tickets from $66 make this one of the best-value nights of the week.

concerts.t: TRAIN – Drops of Jupiter: 25 Years in the Atmosphere
concerts.d: SF's own Train celebrates 25 years of their landmark album at Shoreline — playing the hits for their hometown crowd at one of the Bay's best outdoor venues. Pure nostalgia, summer air, and a setlist you'll know every word to.

concerts.t: Courtney Barnett – Creature of Habit Tour
concerts.d: Two nights of deadpan wit, shaggy storytelling, and sprawling guitar jams from one of indie rock's best live acts. The Fillmore is genuinely the perfect room for her — intimate enough to catch every lyric, big enough to feel the energy.

Sci-fi stage production, orchestral epics, and stadium anthems under the open sky at Shoreline — Muse puts on one of the most visually ambitious live shows in rock, and tickets from $42 make this a genuinely great deal to close the week.

concertsOngoing.t: Roast Battle Bay Area – Cobb's Comedy Club
concertsOngoing.d: Friday Aug 21 at 9:30 PM — verbal sparring at SF's top comedy room, from $28.

concertsOngoing.t: Monét X Change – Cobb's & Punch Line
concertsOngoing.d: Saturday Aug 22 at both venues — double your drag comedy options this weekend.

concertsOngoing.t: Dark and Darker: A Dark Comedy Show – Cobb's
concertsOngoing.d: Sunday Aug 23 at 7:30 PM, from $26 — exactly what it sounds like, and better for it.
Wednesday Aug 26 at 7:30 PM — limited seats from $190, book fast.
Thursday Aug 27 at 8 PM — sharp stand-up at the Financial District room, from $34.
Running through this week at Union Square's premier mid-size stage, from ~$112.

singles.d: Jigsaw Dating takes over Blackbird for a proper speed dating evening — you meet every single in the room one conversation at a time, then a relaxed social hour lets you circle back to your favorites. Well-organized, low-pressure, actually fun.

DateFaster runs a mingle-at-your-own-pace mixer with icebreakers, conversation starters, and a complimentary drink on arrival. Relaxed atmosphere, no awkwardness required. Good option if speed dating feels like too much structure.

Two rooms of hard-hitting Berlin techno at 1015 Folsom — NEUX and softchaos are both making their SF debuts, which gives the night a genuine energy. This is the move if your idea of meeting people involves dancing hard first and talking later.

DSE Runners puts on a $10 timed race nearly every weekend of the year — Golden Gate Park, Lands End, the beach. All levels welcome, runners of all ages, and the post-race hangs tend to be genuinely social. Best kept secret in SF fitness.

Volo runs coed soccer, volleyball, kickball, and basketball across 14 SF neighborhoods — free agents get placed on teams, and post-game bar hangs are basically built into the format. If you're new to the city or just want a weekly crew, this is the move.

SoMa's monthly free block party closes the week on Folsom Street — local food vendors, pop-ups, art, and the kind of easy outdoor hang where conversations start naturally. Zero cover, great energy, and the neighborhood's creative crowd comes out.

singlesOngoing.d: The most complete nightly club and electronic music calendar for SF — check it before any weekend night out.
Casual social runs in the Mission and beyond, multiple days weekly, always free to join.
Kicks off the week Thursday night with deep playa-inspired house and techno, $10 cover, 21+.

date.title: Dinner + Courtney Barnett

steps.title: Dinner near the Fillmore

date.title: JouJou + Daniel Caesar

steps.title: Pre-dinner drinks at True Laurel
steps.detail: Start at one of SF's best cocktail bars in SoMa — inventive seasonal drinks and a low-key cool vibe before the main event.

steps.title: Dinner at JouJou
steps.detail: Oysters, caviar, champagne, and serious buzz from the True Laurel and Lazy Bear team. This is the hottest new table in the city — book ahead.

steps.detail: Uber to Chase Center for night two of the Son of Spergy Tour — 070 Shake opens, Caesar closes it out beautifully. From $88 but buy up for better seats.

solo.title: Museum Morning
solo.tagline: Free art, new installation, no plans required.

steps.title: de Young Museum – Pharaohs
steps.detail: Bay Area residents get free general admission on Saturdays — walk straight into Treasures of the Pharaohs and take your time with 3,000 years of Egyptian history.

steps.title: Picnic at Tunnel Tops
steps.detail: Grab grab-and-go from the new Mess Hall at the Presidio and find a spot at Tunnel Tops with Golden Gate Bridge views.

steps.title: SFMOMA – Jacob Hashimoto: Giant Arc
steps.detail: Head to SFMOMA's Roberts Family Gallery for the brand-new Hashimoto installation — it's free, no ticket needed, and genuinely stunning.

solo.title: Run, Brunch, Indie Rock
solo.tagline: Earn your weekend with a race, fuel up, then catch a great show.

steps.title: DSE Runners Weekend Race
steps.detail: $10 drop-in race at Golden Gate Park or Lands End — all levels welcome, great post-race energy from a genuinely welcoming community.

steps.title: Bar Coto for coffee and a sandwich
steps.detail: Walk-in only at the Cotogna team's Jackson Square café — grab coffee, a great sandwich, and summer gelato while you're at it.

steps.title: Courtney Barnett at the Fillmore
steps.detail: Solo shows at the Fillmore hit differently — you can move around, get close to the stage, and just lose yourself in the music. From $76.

solo.title: Stadium Solo Mission

steps.title: Lucania at the Ferry Building
steps.detail: Pre-show dinner at the A16 team's new southern Italian spot — roasted sardines, pasta, and patio people-watching along the Embarcadero.

steps.title: Walk to Oracle Park
steps.detail: It's a short walk from the Ferry Building to Oracle Park along the waterfront — one of the best pre-show strolls in any city.

steps.title: Noah Kahan – The Great Divide Tour
steps.detail: Resale from ~$401 but this is a once-a-summer kind of night. Grab a beer, find your spot, and let the folk anthems do the rest.

birthday.title: Block Party Birthday
birthday.tagline: Classic cars, street food, and outdoor movies — the free birthday that actually feels special.

steps.title: Hot August Night Block Party – Lower Fillmore
steps.detail: Start the birthday at the neighborhood block party — free entry, classic cars, live entertainment, and food trucks for the whole crew.

steps.title: Zeitgeist Beer Garden
steps.detail: March the group to the Mission's legendary outdoor dive bar for cold pints, sausages, and zero pretension. Classic SF move.

steps.title: Sundown Cinema: The Parent Trap
steps.detail: End the night with the free outdoor movie — bring blankets, bring snacks, and let the birthday person pick the spot.

birthday.title: Fillmore Birthday Weekend
birthday.tagline: A great dinner, the city's best live music room, and a crew that will talk about this one.

steps.title: Group dinner at Tony's Pizza Napoletana
steps.detail: North Beach institution, multiple styles of award-winning pizza, and a festive vibe that works perfectly for a birthday group.

steps.title: Little Stranger + Tropidelic – The Fillmore
steps.detail: Saturday night at the Fillmore — alternative and reggae on the same bill, from $66. The Fillmore's classic concert poster makes a great birthday keepsake (grab one at the box office).

steps.title: After at Vesuvio Café
steps.detail: Close the night at the legendary North Beach dive — Beat Generation history, cheap drinks, and a crowd that loves a good time.

birthday.title: Stadium Birthday
birthday.tagline: Noah Kahan at Oracle Park — hard to top as a birthday night.

steps.title: Pre-show at Charmaine's rooftop
steps.detail: Start with skyline views and strong cocktails at the Proper Hotel rooftop bar — golden hour SF hits different from up here.

steps.title: Dinner at Lucania
steps.detail: Southern Italian at the Ferry Building from the A16 team — great pastas, seafood, and Embarcadero patio energy before walking to the park.

steps.title: Noah Kahan at Oracle Park
steps.detail: The Great Divide Tour at a baseball stadium with the Bay behind it — this is the kind of birthday night people screenshot and remember. Resale from ~$401.

friends.title: Neighborhood Crawl
friends.tagline: Block party, beer garden, then SOMA Nights to close it out.

steps.title: Hot August Night – Lower Fillmore
steps.detail: Kick things off at the free neighborhood block party — classic cars, live entertainment, and street food. Great starting energy for a group.

steps.title: Zeitgeist Beer Garden
steps.detail: The Mission's massive outdoor dive bar is perfect for a group — cold pitchers, communal picnic tables, and no dress code required.

steps.title: SOMA Nights Street Party – Thursday
steps.detail: If you're doing Thursday instead, end the night at the free SoMa block party on Folsom Street — vendors, art, food, and a genuinely fun neighborhood crowd.

friends.title: Muse at Shoreline
friends.tagline: Sci-fi spectacle, outdoor amphitheater, your whole crew — perfect Thursday closer.

steps.title: SOMA Nights Street Party
steps.detail: Start Thursday with the free SoMa block party — grab street food, browse vendors, and use it as the pre-game.

steps.title: Drive south to Shoreline
steps.detail: Carpool down to Mountain View — Shoreline has great tailgate energy and it's worth arriving before the openers.

steps.title: Muse – The Wow! Signal Tour
steps.detail: From $42 — one of rock's most visually ambitious live shows under the open sky at one of the Bay's best outdoor venues. This is a great group show.

friends.title: Techno Night + Late Dinner
friends.tagline: JouJou for dinner, then THROTTLE at 1015 Folsom until sunrise.

steps.title: Dinner at JouJou
steps.detail: Oysters, caviar, and champagne at SoMa's hottest new French seafood restaurant — the perfect pre-club dinner for a group that wants to do the night right.

steps.title: Drinks at True Laurel
steps.detail: The best cocktail bar in SoMa is a five-minute walk from JouJou — creative seasonal drinks and a vibe that transitions perfectly into a late night.

steps.title: THROTTLE at 1015 Folsom
steps.detail: OGUZ, NEUX, and softchaos across two rooms of Berlin-inspired techno. NEUX and softchaos are both making their SF debuts tonight. Go hard.

parents.title: Golden Gate Park & Free Art
parents.tagline: World-class museums, no admission, gorgeous park — the ideal parent itinerary.

steps.title: de Young Museum – Free Saturday
steps.detail: Bay Area residents get free general admission every Saturday — bring a valid ID and walk straight into Treasures of the Pharaohs and Nengi Omuku: The Gathering.

steps.title: Lunch at the Japanese Tea Garden
steps.detail: A short walk through Golden Gate Park to the serene Tea Garden — tea, snacks, and a beautiful setting that parents will genuinely love.

steps.title: SFMOMA – Jacob Hashimoto: Giant Arc (Free)
steps.detail: Head downtown for the brand-new free installation in SFMOMA's Roberts Family Gallery — no ticket required, and it's a genuinely impressive piece to walk through together.

parents.title: Waterfront Day & The Etruscans
parents.tagline: Ferry Building lunch, Legion of Honor exhibit, and a sunset view to send them home happy.

steps.title: Brunch at Lucania – Ferry Building
steps.detail: Southern Italian right at the Ferry Building from the A16 team — great pasta and seafood, plus the iconic Embarcadero patio for people-watching.

steps.title: Legion of Honor – The Etruscans
steps.detail: Drive up to the Legion of Honor for this world-class exhibit on ancient Italian civilization — open through September 20, and the museum's location at Land's End has unbeatable views.

steps.title: Sunset at Lands End Lookout
steps.detail: Walk the short trail to the Lands End Lookout after the exhibit — Golden Gate Bridge views at golden hour. This is the SF moment parents tell everyone about.

parents.title: TRAIN Homecoming at Shoreline
parents.tagline: A classic SF band, an outdoor amphitheater, and a setlist everyone knows every word to.

steps.title: Afternoon at the Asian Art Museum
steps.detail: Over 18,000 works spanning the full breadth of Asian art history — a genuinely world-class collection at Civic Center, perfect for a leisurely afternoon visit.

steps.title: Early dinner at Bix
steps.detail: Supper club glamour in a Gold Rush–era alley in Jackson Square — martinis, duck confit, and the kind of warm, grown-up atmosphere that parents absolutely love.

steps.title: TRAIN at Shoreline Amphitheatre
steps.detail: SF's hometown band celebrates 25 years of Drops of Jupiter in Mountain View — a nostalgic, feel-good night at one of the Bay's best outdoor venues. They will sing every word.
